note: Four thousand years of settlement in one place — Bronze Age huts through to a Norse farm. Allow a good hour and a half.
The islands' story under one roof, down at Hay's Dock. Café on site. The obvious answer to a wet afternoon.
A restored 1870s croft house with the fire lit — thatched roof, box beds, and a water mill down the burn.
A laird's house in Northmavine turned local museum — fishing, crofting and the folk of the north end.
Yell's oldest building, now a museum and gallery with a tearoom.
A shed full of traditional Shetland boats, kept as they were built and used.
Fair Isle and lace knitting at the Böd of Gremista — the work close up, and often someone knitting.
The Shetland Bus story, next to the castle — the wartime runs to occupied Norway.
A restored Victorian watermill in the south end, machinery and all.
Local history, knitwear and a tearoom — an easy stop on the road south.
The 18th-century fort above Lerwick harbour. Walk the walls for the view over Bressay Sound.
Lerwick's theatre — worth checking what's on while you're here.
A small exhibition at Sandsayre pier, where the Mousa boat goes from.
